_comment: Mutation spec for S21 (cold-open assembly), task 6.7.
The spec names the highest-risk item first and it is right to: 'assume monotonic keeps in
assembly rebasing'. That is monotonic_rebase below. An assembly produces [hook, body] where the
hook's source times come AFTER the body's, so a rebase that sorts the keeps places the hook's
captions at the body's timeline positions. Captions still appear, still look like captions, and
are attached to the wrong words -- it gets blamed on the ASR long before anyone suspects the edit.
duplicate_rebase is the same defect's quieter half, and it is the one this implementation had to
introduce a new function for. `filler.rebase_words` stops at the first keep containing a word.
With the lifted line RETAINED, its source range is in the keep list twice -- so the line is
captioned on its first airing and silent on its second. Nothing errors and nothing looks broken.
Three of these survived their first run and each exposed a real test gap rather than a
false alarm, which is recorded per mutation below because the gap is the interesting part:
pipeline_monotonic_rebase -- every test called the module directly, so the CALL SITE was
untested; and the first fix was still vacuous because the fixture
script repeats ordinary words like 'the', so 'some word appears
twice' is true whichever rebase ran. Only a word that occurs
exactly once in the source can distinguish heard-twice from
written-twice.
composition_dropped       -- counting one re-encode cannot see whether the filler keeps were
honoured. Needed an independent containment check against the
filler plan, captured separately (R9.9).
refusal_silenced          -- no test drove the pipeline into a refusal at all.

mutations.name: monotonic_rebase
mutations.old:
for keep in keeps:
        offsets.append((keep.start, keep.end, offset))
mutations.new:
for keep in sorted(keeps, key=lambda k: k.start):
        offsets.append((keep.start, keep.end, offset))
mutations.why: The item the spec calls the highest risk in all four specs. Sorting the keeps re-imposes source order, so the hook's words are offset as though the hook still played where it was recorded. Every caption still renders, at a plausible time, against the wrong speech.

mutations.name: duplicate_rebase
mutations.why: Restores `filler.rebase_words`' behaviour. A retained cold open has its source range in the keep list twice; stopping at the first match captions the first airing and leaves the second silent, which reads as an ASR gap.

mutations.name: pipeline_monotonic_rebase
mutations.why: The call site rather than the seam. The duplicate-aware rebase existing does not mean the pipeline chose it, and this survived until a test asserted on the words the compositor is actually handed.

mutations.name: composition_dropped
mutations.why: R2.3. The assembly would be rendered without the filler and U4 removals folded in, so words the user struck out come back -- while the re-encode count stays at one, which is why counting passes cannot catch it.

mutations.name: keep_list_resorted
mutations.why: `_merge` sorts by start and coalesces. Correct for filler removal, catastrophic for an assembly: it silently converts the edit back into the contiguous clip it was lifted from, and also merges the duplicate range into one.

mutations.name: video_reordered_alone
mutations.why: R2.7. `trim` and `atrim` take separate arguments, so a copy-paste error produces a clip whose audio and video are each internally coherent and mutually wrong -- the picture shows one moment while the sound plays another.

mutations.name: dangling_opener_lifted
mutations.why: R1.6. The cold open is the one position where a back-reference cannot resolve, because nothing came before it. A hook opening on 'and that's exactly why he quit' is worse than no hook at all.

mutations.name: already_first_reordered
mutations.why: R1.5. Lifting the first sentence to the front reorders an already-correct clip and, when retained, duplicates its opening line for no reason.

mutations.name: no_signal_precedence_inverted
mutations.why: `text_signal` is sparse, so on a flat clip every sentence ties at zero and the earlier-index tiebreak returns sentence 0. Reported as 'already_first' that is a false claim about the material: nothing stood out, which is a different finding from correct ordering.

mutations.name: refusal_silenced
mutations.why: R2.9. A refusal nobody can see is indistinguishable from the feature being off, and the operator concludes the setting does nothing.
